slots.title: Tesla closes up 3.4% after Q3 print
slots.body:

The company reported Q3 EPS of $0.48 versus a $0.45 estimate and revenue of about $28.05 billion versus roughly $28.06 billion expected.

Earnings coverage framed the quarter as profit beating expectations even as revenue tracked near the forecast.

slots.title: U.S. cash session — Oct. 21, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 rose 0.6% to 7,757.85 (+45.28 points).
The Nasdaq Composite gained 1.1% to 26,702.86 (+278.04).
The Dow added 0.7% to 52,856.09 (+360.21).
The Russell 2000 edged up 0.2% to 2,781.02.

The CBOE Volatility Index fell 3.6% to 16.68, down 0.63 point from the prior close.

Healthcare led Nasdaq sector averages, up about 1.3% on the day.
Real estate lagged, down about 1.1%.
Utilities rose about 0.7%; consumer defensive about 0.8%.
Technology averaged about +0.4%; communication services about -0.4%; energy about -0.2%.

Earnings dominated the narrative.
Tesla ($TSLA) finished up 3.4% at 386.47 after Q3 EPS of $0.48 versus a $0.45 estimate.
Meta ($META) closed up 0.5% at 697.52 despite EPS of $3.83 versus a $6.54 estimate, with revenue near $64.6 billion above the roughly $63.3 billion forecast.
IBM ($IBM) gained 3.9% to 251.46 on EPS $2.95 versus $2.85 expected and revenue above estimate.
Danaher ($DHR) rose 4.4% to 234.09; Texas Instruments ($TXN) +2.5% to 284.65; Thermo Fisher ($TMO) +1.0% to 694.02.

AT&T ($T) fell 6.4% to 21.91 even with EPS $0.65 versus $0.60 expected and revenue above estimate, on volume near 83.7 million shares.
Alphabet ($GOOGL) lost 1.6% to 334.76.
Oracle ($ORCL) -1.6% to 129.10.
Lam Research ($LRCX) reported EPS $2.20 versus $2.18 expected but closed down 1.0% at 260.81.
Apple ($AAPL) rose 1.3% to 343.99 with a session high of 345.22 against a 52-week high of 348.15 in the quote data.

Taiwan Semiconductor ($TSM) gained 1.6% to 431.89.
Alibaba ($BABA) declined 3.9% to 104.40.
Procter & Gamble ($PG) and AbbVie ($ABBV) each closed about -1.5%.

The Energy Information Administration reported a 3.061 million-barrel draw in U.S. crude oil stocks for the week of Oct. 16, compared with a -0.8 million-barrel estimate, and a 2.952 million-barrel drop in gasoline stocks versus a -0.4 million estimate.

Brent crude rose 1.6% to 110.52.
Gold futures slipped 0.5% to 4,128.00.
The United States Oil Fund ($USO proxy in tape) closed down 0.5% at 159.80.
Bitcoin ($BTCUSD) fell 1.5% to 82,730.23.

Overseas indexes were softer: Hang Seng -2.6% to 23,041.00; Nikkei 225 -1.1% to 63,917.43.
FTSE 100 +0.2% to 10,752.88.

Latest Treasury snapshot in the feed (dated 2026-10-19) showed the 10-year at 5.2% and the 2s10s spread at 0.38 percentage point.
The dollar-tracking fund in the cross-asset set ($UUP) ticked up 0.1% to 28.92.
